chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Commander of the Faithful disliked bartering meat with an animal.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.بِالْحَيَوَانِ: With the animal (bartering meat for a live animal)
key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked (expressed a juristic preference, not prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali dislike regarding the exchange of meat and animals?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* records Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) dislike (*karah*) for bartering meat directly with a live animal, a practice often associated with the pre-Islamic *Nasi’ah* or deferred exchange. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects a caution against *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding the quality and quantity of the meat relative to the live animal, ensuring fairness in trade. It underscores the Imam’s emphasis on precise valuation and clarity in commercial transactions to prevent exploitation.
